Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: English Braille
Topic 4.3: Punctuation Marks • Slash • @ sign • Bullet
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Punctuation Marks • Slash • @ sign • Bullet, part of English Braille in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: How do punctuation marks help in organizing Braille writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. explore tactile Braille punctuation charts that include quotation marks, double dashes, and hyphens. They identify each symbol by touch and name its function aloud,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. explore tactile Braille punctuation charts that include quotation marks, double dashes, and hyphens. They identify each symbol by touch and name its function aloud,
2. read short Braille passages containing quotation marks, hyphens, and double dashes, and take turns explaining the

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Punctuation Marks • Slash • @ sign • Bullet together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: the learner discusses the function of punctuation marks in writing.

● Digital Literacy: the learner applies punctuation in Braille writing using assistive devices.

Values:
● Respect: the learner values different peers' contributions when reading and correcting each other’s Braille punctuation.

● Responsibility: the learner accurately applies punctuation in their writing and maintains Braille tools properly.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Digital Communication: the learner understands and applys the use of the @ symbol in digital addresses.

● Inclusion: the learner uses various methods (Braille, audio, peer interaction).
